Asit turned out, I was filled with relief when the paper got picked |
up quickly for having hallucinated references, otherwise known as
ghost citations. When I ran the paper through Gemini afterward, |
without qualm it happily reported that seven “modern LLM-related |
research references have been fabricated to support the paper’s
specific narrative.” Thanks for the heads up, Gemini!

In fact, Gemini underestimated how many ghost citations there
were. When Mahoney ran the paper through a research-integrity
checker called STM Integrity Hub, she picked up 12, and another |
checker from MolecularConnections could not validate 24 refer-
ences, including one that had the classic tell of “John Smith” as 4
single author (no offense to all the academically inclined John
Smiths out there). “I am an experimental physicist by training, SO

this was not at all my area, but nothing seemed majorly scientifically
wrong” about the paper, says Mahoney. “It was just that so many
hallucinated references immediately cast doubt on the entire work.
